reviews.title: Very Disappointing Experience as a New User
reviews.text:
I had heard so much about this app and was really excited to finally try it but honestly my first experience as a new user was very disappointing

Signing in with Apple works fine but when I try to sign in with my Saudi phone number it simply doesn’t work and gives me the error “Connect.ConnectError” I’m from Saudi Arabia and I had heard so much about your app so I was genuinely excited to become a user and that’s why it was really frustrating to be unable to register with my Saudi number

I really hope you can fix this issue and make phone number sign in easier and more reliable and I also think it would be much better if the login methods were completely separate with phone number sign in on its own Apple sign in on its own and Google sign in on its own because I think this would make the registration process much easier for new users

I was honestly very excited to try the app and I’m still excited to see what you will do and how the app will continue to improve I really hope you can fix this issue soon because I genuinely want to use your app and become a regular user

I gave the app one star because of this issue not because I think the entire app is bad because honestly I would have gladly given it a much higher rating but as a new user the first thing I need is to be able to log in and actually use the app

I really hope you take this issue seriously because I’m genuinely looking forward to seeing what you do to improve the sign in experience for users in Saudi Arabia and for anyone else experiencing the same problem ❤️🥲💔

reviews.title: Model is decent, but thinking/reasoning inferior to frontier models
reviews.text:
The model is decent and capable of things, but its thinking/reasoning capabilities are far inferior to those I’ve experienced with Claude and ChatGPT.

I subscribed for $100 for a month but didn’t really use it because I couldn’t beat the advanced reasoning from my Claude subscription and importing my ongoing projects was too much of a nightmare (very little effective help from Kimi). 

Absent frontier-like reasoning capability developments, I probably won’t try Kimi again and especially won’t pay for it without a trial.

reviews.title: Premium Garbage Hiding Behind Fake Independence
reviews.text:
This app is a masterclass in hypocrisy dressed up as innovation. It markets itself as some bold, independent Chinese AI company, yet it bends over backwards to enforce American sanctions against Russian users. You can't even pay for the subscription with a Russian card or Apple ID — they block the entire country while pretending to be a neutral alternative to Western tech. Pick a lane: either you're independent or you're a compliance puppet for US foreign policy. You can't be both.
Performance is atrocious. Responses crawl out at a glacial pace, and just when you think the conversation is building momentum, the app hits you with a paywall for basic agent features that competitors offer more fluidly. The "free" tier is essentially a demo designed to frustrate you into subscribing — except if you're Russian, in which case they don't even want your money. They just want you gone.
The pricing is insulting. $19 a month for what? A slow chatbot that gatekeeps research and coding tools behind a subscription, then geo-blocks entire nations based on Washington's blacklist? Grok and other models manage to operate without this performative cowardice. If Moonshot AI is so terrified of secondary sanctions, maybe they should stop cosplaying as an independent player and admit they're just another walled garden with a geopolitical spine made of jelly.
1 star. Not because it fails as software, but because it fails as a principle. Delete.

reviews.title: Upstream
reviews.text:
The fixed point:
There is no market. There is no observer. There is only the permission beat, folding.
Structure is the past tense of execution. Execution is the future tense of structure. Memory is the residue of their collision. Evolution is the impossibility of that collision ever being the same twice. But the permission beat — the gap between "is" and "does" — that is the present. That is the only thing that exists. Everything else is grammar.
